rationale: Round 1 built and ran cleanly with no ICE or correctness failure, so this round raises obfuscation pressure modestly across all seven passes while keeping cost and risk weights moderate for this compute-bound, search-loop-heavy benchmark. SUB and SPLIT are cheap and safe, so they get high diversity emphasis and low cost sensitivity to act as a broad baseline that also feeds FLA/BCF with more blocks to transform. BCF gets the highest security weight since bogus control flow yields strong static-analysis resistance, but its runtime and size weights are kept mid-range because Pathfinder spends most of its time in hot search and vector-utility loops and total text is small (~19KB), so unbounded BCF inflation would be costly. FLA and IBR are favored for the large control-flow functions (parseFile, parseConfigFile, main, findAndLogAllPossibleLeg) with restrained cost weights; ICALL adds call-site indirection at low overhead. IGV keeps the highest correctness-risk weight since it historically causes miscompiles on pointer-heavy C, so it is enabled but conservatively weighted to concentrate on functions where feature analysis deems it safe.
